note: ADR-019 / ADR-017 am. 1 FORWARD DEPTH CAMERA -- the second aperture, separate from the ADR-007 nadir NDVI rig, that buys the detection lead time a nadir camera geometrically cannot (ADR-017 am. 1 measured `speed_at_which_nadir_becomes_safe_mps = None`: nadir's 2.480 m forward horizon would have to be 17.8-38.8 m). Consumed by scripts/gen_farm_world.py, which emits a SECOND link + fixed joint on the same wrapped iris_with_gimbal -- do not hand-edit the generated SDF, edit this file and regenerate. NOTHING in this file may change config/ndvi_camera.json or the ADR-007 mount: NDVI is FROZEN for the duration of the ag-avoidance push (ADR-019 item 7) and its mount is live-verified (2.2 px, scripts/verify_mount_geometry.sh).

mount.note: A SECOND rigid link on the same wrapper model (iris_with_gimbal_ndvi), attached by the same nested-model + <joint type='fixed'> mechanism ADR-007 proved live on 2026-08-05. Separate LINK, not a second sensor on the NDVI link: the two apertures point 90 degrees apart, so they cannot share a pose, and touching the NDVI link is exactly the re-opening ADR-019 forbids. Like the NDVI mount this link carries sensors only -- no <visual>, no <collision> -- so it can never occlude either camera.
mount.parent_link_scoped_source: IDENTICAL to config/ndvi_camera.json's, and for the identical reason (iris_with_gimbal pulls model://iris_with_standoffs in with <include merge="true">, which FLATTENS base_link into iris_with_gimbal instead of keeping an iris_with_standoffs:: sub-scope). That name is the one CONFIRMED LIVE on 2026-08-05 Gate 0 after the fully-nested spelling was rejected by gz sim; reusing it is why this mount owes no scoped-name discovery of its own.
mount.mount_pose_translation_note: x=+0.15 m: forward of everything on the airframe. The iris rotor arms reach x = +/-0.13 m (ardupilot_gazebo iris_with_standoffs rotor placement) so the aperture sits 0.02 m ahead of the frontmost rotor hub, and the horizontal frustum only reaches |y| = 0.22 m (a rotor's lateral offset) at 0.357 m AHEAD of the camera -- i.e. the props are geometrically outside the cone, not merely assumed to be. y=0 puts the optical axis in the airframe's plane of symmetry so a range measurement carries no cross-track bias. z=0 keeps it at base_link height, 0.08 m ABOVE the nadir NDVI mount and above model://gimbal_small_3d, which hangs below the nose. Self-occlusion by the airframe mesh is the one part of this that host-side math cannot settle -- it is a LIVE gate (docs/runbooks/FORWARD_DEPTH_SENSOR.md, gate D2: no finite depth pixel nearer than 1.0 m with the vehicle parked in the open).
mount.mount_pose_rpy_note: rpy (0,0,0) -- and that is the WHOLE derivation, which is precisely why it needs writing down. Gazebo camera sensors look along the SENSOR FRAME's +X, with optical x (image u+) = sensor -Y and optical y (image v+) = sensor -Z. At identity that gives: optical z (into the scene) = body +X = FORWARD; optical u+ = body -Y = the vehicle's right; optical v+ = body -Z = down. Correct forward camera, standard image handedness, zero rotation. THE TRAP, named because this project already paid for it once: the 'obvious' ROS/pinhole answer for a forward camera is rpy (-pi/2, 0, -pi/2), which under Gazebo's +X convention aims the optical axis at body -Y -- the camera looks out of the RIGHT FLANK. It would still return a perfectly plausible frame (ground below, tree rows across, sky above), which is exactly why a VALUE-only gate cannot catch it; what catches it is geometry, and both halves are gated: the host check asserts the axis is body +X, and the in-render D2 RANGE+AIM pair reads a known target at a known range in a known pixel. That is the same class of bug as ADR-007 am. 5 (the nadir mount faced the horizon for two weeks under four green gates). Gated up front, host-side, by scripts/check_depth_mount.py, whose cross-check is that the SAME general rpy->optical-axis formula, evaluated at config/ndvi_camera.json's live-verified (-pi/2, +pi/2, 0), must reproduce ndvi_georef.CAMERA_TO_BODY_SIGNS exactly.
mount.tilt_rejected_note: A downward tilt was considered and REJECTED, with the geometry: the ADR-019 threat band is +/-6 m around a 15 m cruise, and at fy=520.006 / cy=240 the vertical half-FOV is 24.775 deg, so a LEVEL camera contains the entire +/-6 m band at every range beyond 6*fy/cy = 13.00 m -- which sits well below the 17.8-38.8 m horizon the replay actually requires. A 10 deg down-tilt would pull the band's lower edge in to 8.64 m but push its UPPER edge out to 22.74 m, i.e. it trades coverage this design does not need for a hole inside the required horizon. Level is also the only pose with no tilt constant to get wrong. UNMEASURED and named as such: a copter pitches nose-down to cruise, which rotates this camera with it; measuring the actual cruise pitch and re-checking band coverage against it is a LIVE item (FORWARD_DEPTH_SENSOR.md gate D6), NOT something to pre-compensate for with an invented tilt.
mount.mount_inertia_note: Same values, same reason, as config/ndvi_camera.json's mount: physics engines need valid inertial properties on every link even for a fixed-joint accessory, and 0.05 kg is negligible against the airframe. Deliberately identical rather than re-derived -- two accessory links of the same kind should not carry two different invented masses.

camera.note: Intrinsics DELIBERATELY IDENTICAL to config/ndvi_camera.json's (640x480, hfov 1.1033 rad -> fx=fy=520.006 px). Not laziness: one pinhole model in the repo means the projection primitives, the resolvability arithmetic and every cross-check read one set of numbers, and CameraIntrinsics.from_config already reproduces this pair. A WIDER lens was the alternative and it loses: halving fx halves the range at which a 0.18 m bird still spans the 2.0 px the adopted morphology needs (46.8 m -> 23.4 m), and buys coverage for crossing threats this world does not contain (bird_1 z=8 m and bird_2 z=6 m are both OUTSIDE the +/-6 m threat band at a 15 m cruise; bird_0, the only bird that enters the cylinder, closes head-on down lane x=15 at zero cross-track offset).
camera.horizontal_fov_note: fx = (640/2)/tan(1.1033/2) = 520.0058 px; vertical FOV = 2*atan(240/520.0058) = 49.550 deg, i.e. +/-24.775 deg. Same value as the NDVI pair, which came from sim/spike/scenario_default.json's pinhole intrinsics.
camera.update_rate_note: Matched to the ADR-007 pair, on evidence rather than symmetry. 5.0 Hz is the ONLY camera rate this stack has measured end-to-end at 100 % delivery (ADR-013 am. 9, Fast DDS SHM segment + --shm-size=1g; painting cadence 5.0 Hz flat), and 2.0 Hz was measured 16x WORSE, not better (config/ndvi_camera.json update_rate_note -- delivery here is bursty, not steadily rate-limited). Raising it to buy lead time was considered and NOT taken: the whole cost of the 5 Hz tick is one frame period, 0.200 s, which scripts/predict_forward_lead.py already carries as an explicit line item in the latency budget, and the gate PASSES with that 0.200 s in it. Doubling the rate would add a third full render pass per tick to a software-rendered (llvmpipe, no GPU passthrough) pipeline to buy 0.1 s the budget does not need. Revisit only if the live acquisition range measures short.
camera.clip_note: near 0.1 m matches the NDVI pair and is deliberately SMALL: gz writes -inf for anything nearer than near-clip, so a large near clip would hide airframe self-occlusion from the very gate (D2) that exists to catch it. far 60.0 m is chosen to sit ABOVE the sensor's physical acquisition limit and BELOW the world: 46.80 m is where a 0.18 m bird stops spanning the 2.0 px radius the adopted morphology needs (see detection.min_resolving_radius_px), so the horizon is set by physics and not by a config number -- a far clip below 46.8 m would make THIS FILE the thing that limits detection while looking like a rendering detail. 60 m is also below the 96 m field diagonal (75x60 m, config/field_polygon.json), so the far half of the world never enters a frame. THE TWO CULLS ARE NOT SYMMETRIC, and only stating one of them is how the headroom got overstated by an order of magnitude: the NEAR cull is on the stored Z-depth (`point.x < near + tolerance`), while the FAR cull is on the EUCLIDEAN length of the camera-space point (`length(point) > far - tolerance`), both in gz-rendering8 ogre2 depth_camera_fs.glsl, and the VALUE stored either way is the pinhole Z-depth (`point.x = -viewSpacePos.z`). So `far` bounds SLANT range: the effective Z-depth horizon is far/|ray|, which is 60/1.174 = 51.10 m at the horizontal frame edge and 60/1.262 = 47.56 m at the CORNER. Against the 46.80 m acquisition bound that is 1.6 % of headroom at the corner, NOT the 28 % the on-axis 60 m suggests. Gated: scripts/check_depth_mount.py asserts acquisition <= the corner bound, and the in-render D2 CULL probe measures it (the greatest finite Z-depth in a frame is far/|ray| at its own pixel, ~57.8 m, not 60.0).
camera.camera_info_topic_note: DERIVED, NOT DECLARED -- and this is the one gz-sensors fact most likely to be got wrong by analogy with the ADR-007 block. `<camera_info_topic>` is read in CameraSensor::Load (gz-sensors8 src/CameraSensor.cc:389), and DepthCameraSensor::Load does NOT call it -- it calls the base Sensor::Load and then AdvertiseInfo() with an EMPTY infoTopic (src/DepthCameraSensor.cc:249,297). AdvertiseInfo() then derives the name by splitting <topic> on '/', POPPING THE LAST SEGMENT and appending '/camera_info' (src/CameraSensor.cc:662-676). So `<topic>fg/depth/image` yields exactly `/fg/depth/camera_info`, and emitting a `<camera_info_topic>` element here would be dead config that LOOKS live -- the same failure mode as a `qos:` key in sim/bridge/fg_sensor_bridge.yaml. The generator therefore emits <topic> only, and the derived name is a LIVE gate (FORWARD_DEPTH_SENSOR.md gate D1).

depth.gz_sensor_type_note: sdformat14 accepts 'depth' or 'depth_camera' (src/Sensor.cc:294); 'depth_camera' is spelled out. `rgbd_camera` was the alternative and was REJECTED: it renders an extra colour pass per frame that nothing consumes (ADR-003 am. 10 measured that a second visible band co-located with the first buys exactly zero -- gap +0.000), on a software renderer, for a stream the nadir RGB already provides. RADAR is refused at a higher level: ADR-019 item 5 researched and rejected it (no gz-sim radar sensor exists, and a ray-cast proxy cannot reproduce the >35 dB specular RCS cliff that makes real radar wire-detection work).
depth.encoding_note: DepthCameraSensor publishes gz.msgs.Image with pixel_format_type R_FLOAT32 (src/DepthCameraSensor.cc:585); ros_gz at the pinned SHA 9d7f8c721c233a9ac8b43950129d51e67905523e maps R_FLOAT32 -> ROS encoding '32FC1' (ros_gz_bridge/src/convert/sensor_msgs.cpp:158-159). One float per pixel, 640*480*4 = 1,228,800 B per frame -- 19 fragments at the 65,384 B SHM fragment size, the same size class as the fused /fg/ndvi/image stream that the ADR-013 am. 9 segment fix was sized for.
depth.value_semantics: PINHOLE Z-DEPTH IN METRES along the optical axis -- not slant range. gz-rendering8 ogre2 depth_camera_fs.glsl stores `point.x = -viewSpacePos.z`, which is the perpendicular distance to the image plane. This is the SAME quantity ndvi_georef.pixel_at_depth_to_enu already takes as `depth_m`, so the un-projection primitive is reused rather than re-derived.
depth.no_return_semantics: +inf for anything beyond far clip, -inf for anything nearer than near clip (gz-rendering8 Ogre2DepthCamera dataMaxVal/dataMinVal default to +/-gz::math::INF_D, passed to the shader as the `max`/`min` uniforms). A non-finite pixel is therefore a REFUSAL, not a range, and the detection path must drop it -- never clamp it to the clip plane, which would report a confident obstacle at exactly 60 m. DepthDetectionSource's range window is EXCLUSIVE at both ends for the same reason: a clip plane is where gz stops measuring, not the last place it measures, so a depth of exactly 60.0 or exactly 0.1 IS the clamp signature and is refused. Measured in the render, not only source-read: FORWARD_DEPTH_SENSOR.md gates D2 NEAR (literal '-inf') and D2 FAR.
depth.noise_note: gz-sensors' own default (no <noise> element = no noise), kept DELIBERATELY and recorded as a transfer gap rather than papered over. DepthCameraSensor supports Gaussian noise only (src/DepthCameraSensor.cc, 'The depth camera sensor only supports Gaussian noise'), and this repo has no measured stddev for any real depth sensor -- inventing one would be a constant from prose, and every gate number downstream would then depend on it. A noiseless depth camera is OPTIMISTIC in the same direction as eval/point_mass.py's unmodelled dynamics: it belongs in the transfer-gap register (proposed TG-6), next to TG-1..5, not in this file as a guessed number. The day a real datasheet exists, the element is four lines of generator.

detection.note: Sensor-side quantities the ADR-019 booking gate (scripts/predict_forward_lead.py) reads. They describe what the OPTICS can deliver; what the detector then does with it is src/fieldguard_planning/depth_detect.py's business.
detection.min_resolving_radius_source: MEASURED, not asserted: the smallest apparent radius at which a filled disc still survives the ADOPTED morphology (ndvi_detect.detect_blobs -- 3x3 binary open then close, then DEFAULT_MIN_AREA=6) at the WORST sub-pixel placement swept over offsets {0, 0.25, 0.5} px in both axes. r=1.9 px (9 raw px) is erased by the opening; r=2.0 px (13 raw px) survives at every offset. Re-measured on every test run by tests/fieldguard_planning/test_depth_detect.py so the constant cannot drift from the code that produced it. Mirrored in src/fieldguard_planning/depth_detect.MIN_RESOLVING_RADIUS_PX, which is the importable copy; this entry exists so the config is readable on its own, and the test pins the two equal. DISCLOSED LIMITATION: detect_blobs is the NDVI detector's morphology, used here because it is the only morphology this repo has ever scored. The DEPTH segmenter does not exist yet and may not use it, so this floor -- and therefore the 46.80 m geometric bound derived from it -- inherits an assumption from a different detector. Re-measuring the floor against whatever the segmenter actually runs is BOOKED for the segmenter session (FORWARD_DEPTH_SENSOR.md Known gaps).
detection.acquisition_range_note: range = fx * r_object / r_px, so a 0.18 m bird (config/birds/farm_world_birds.json, all three) reaches the 2.0 px floor at 520.0058 * 0.18 / 2.0 = 46.80 m. That is a GEOMETRIC UPPER BOUND from the pinhole model plus the morphology -- it is NOT a render measurement, and gz's depth camera runs SetAntiAliasing(2), whose effect on a 4-px target's depth values at 46 m is unknown. ADR-019 item 6 requires the booking gate to run on the sensor's OWN live camera_info and measured horizon, never on config prose, which is why scripts/predict_forward_lead.py takes --acq-range-m: measure it (FORWARD_DEPTH_SENSOR.md gate D3), feed it in, re-run the gate, THEN book.

booking_gate.note: ADR-019 item 6, the no-failure-theater tripwire. Only the two numbers that are NOT owned elsewhere live here; everything else is imported so it cannot drift. The 3.00 m bar comes from avoidance_policy.PolicyParams.min_bird_clearance_m, the plant from eval/point_mass.GUIDED_DEFAULT, the bird speed from config/birds/farm_world_birds.json via check_live_flight_log.max_bird_speed_m_s, and the frame period from camera.update_rate_hz above.
booking_gate.lead_margin_factor_source: ADR-019 item 6 / Ruling 002 tripwire (a), verbatim: '>=1.3x lead-time margin under guided_default'.
booking_gate.control_tick_latency_source: The MEASURED median executor tick on the flown stack, n=1855 (ADR-016 am. 1, re-derived from the committed logs by test rather than from the nominal 5 Hz). Added to one camera frame period (1/update_rate_hz = 0.200 s, the worst-case wait for the next depth frame) to form the pipeline latency the gate subtracts from the available lead. NOT included and named as such: AUTO->GUIDED mode-switch latency, which is transfer-gap TG-5 and remains unmeasured -- so the budget below is optimistic by exactly that unknown.
